claim: SME-style mapping yields candidate inferences that are only surmises; a separate process must check truth, and the built-in check is thin (only drops permuted copies of known non-commutative facts).
agent_test: Compare: model transfers freely vs transfers then a code or test check accepts or rejects each conjecture; count wrong conjectures kept, at equal tokens.

claim: People prefer to carry over facts that hang off a shared causal system (systematicity) over equally plausible isolated facts. Shown in two labs: Clement and Gentner 1991 (3 experiments) and Markman 1997 (4 experiments).
agent_test: Rank candidate inferences by attachment to the mapped chain; compare accuracy of kept inferences vs unranked, same token budget.

claim: Grounding rule: transfer only source facts connected to relations already mapped; ungrounded surface-similar facts are the main error source.
agent_test: Tag each conjecture grounded or ungrounded; measure error rate of each class on held-out checkable tasks.

claim: Humans keep one-to-one mapping when inferring: zero inconsistent object substitutions in four studies. A cheap code check can enforce it.
agent_test: Code check that no source element maps to two target elements; count violations the model makes with and without the check.

claim: Humans also produce inferences not in the source at a rate similar to shared-system ones (Markman Exp 1: 0.56 other vs 0.52 shared). Candidates should be tagged copied or invented.
agent_test: Tag provenance of each conjecture; test whether invented ones are less often true.

claim: Overall mapping similarity is a poor stand-in for trust in one specific inference: a shared preventer raises similarity but lowers the effect inference (GG 89.4 vs GGP 74.4 effect rating at similarity 6.35 vs 7.53). Original Lee and Holyoak 2008 was not opened. Gap search: the abstracts of Lee and Holyoak 2008 (3 experiments) and Holyoak, Lee and Lu 2010 confirm the direction (removing a shared preventer lowers similarity and raises judged inductive strength); full text and cell values still unopened.
agent_test: Score each conjecture separately from the whole mapping; check whether mapping score predicts conjecture truth.

claim: Whether transfer and truth evaluation are one process (causal-model account) or two (SME plus later causal calculation) is disputed between Lee and Holyoak and Colhoun and Gentner. Only one side's text was opened. Gap search: the Lee and Holyoak side was read at abstract level only; they claim analogical inference runs through a causal model.
agent_test: Not decidable from text; design the agent with two steps anyway and ablate the second.

claim: Structure-guided inference weakens when the source is out of view or only remembered (Exp 3 effect 0.92 vs 0.13, smaller than Exp 2 1.63 vs 0).
agent_test: Keep source text verbatim in context vs paraphrased summary; compare conjecture accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: LLM letter-string rule transfer is brittle when the alphabet is changed: humans .753 overall vs GPT-3 .488, GPT-3.5 .350, GPT-4 .452 (Lewis and Mitchell); Hodel and West found the same for GPT-3; Stevenson et al. found loss from Latin to symbol alphabets in GPT-4o (.85 to .48), Claude-3.5 (.68 to .46) with humans flat (.88 to .89).
agent_test: Always test an inference rule on a mutated surface variant; report pass rate on original vs mutated at equal tokens.

claim: Cause of the letter-string failure is disputed: Webb et al. show GPT-4 with self-written code reaches about human accuracy (46% of GPT-4 errors valid alternative rule vs 39% for humans), saying the failure is counting not analogy; critics say familiarity or contamination. Code sample was small (60 per interval). Gap search: Webb, Holyoak and Lu (2024) reply says models also generalise to counterfactual variants, so the dispute is still live; no paired with/without-code test on other mutated task families was found (REL tool test d05 is not paired).
agent_test: Route index and counting steps to code and compare with model-only on mutated items.

claim: Far-domain structural analogy is hard for LLMs while near is easier: ARN near 75.0% vs far 39.6% (humans 97.9 / 94.1); StoryAnalogy ChatGPT about 30% vs humans 85.7%; GPT-3 story analogies far not above chance (p=0.065). GPT-4 in 2023 was better (unquantified). Gap search (2025-26 models): reasoning and frontier models still fall far below humans on related transfer tasks (o3-mini 86.6 to 17.0 and R1 80.6 to 23.2 on noisy Raven; top models 39.8 vs humans 68.5 on A2RBench; Claude Opus 4.5 and Gemini 3 Pro at chance on high relational-complexity matrices). ARN itself and StoryAnalogy were not re-run on 2025-26 models. Also StoryAnalogy correction: ChatGPT about 30 percent, other cells to 44.2, best model about 48 percent.
agent_test: Build far-source and near-decoy items; measure how often the agent transfers from a surface-similar wrong source, with and without a structure check.

claim: LLM analogy judgements are order- and wording-sensitive: GPT-4 correct story 1.0 first vs 0.72 second; Permuted Pairs drops LLMs (coef -1.7 to -2.3, p<.001) but not humans; prompt wording moves accuracy from about 20% to about 100%; typos cost 3-7% relative.
agent_test: Randomise order and paraphrase every mapping prompt; report variance across variants.

claim: Analogical prompting (model writes related solved problems first) gives modest gains over 0-shot CoT: about +4% average; Codeforces GPT-3.5 Acc@1 8 / 9 / 11 / 13 / 15 for 0-shot / CoT / 3-shot / exemplars / exemplars+knowledge, GPT-4 16 / 16 / 17 / 17 / 19. Uses more output tokens; no equal-token comparison. Gap search: Qin et al. (2025) find random self-generated examples match or beat relevant ones on math (GPT-3.5 average relevant 52.4 vs no-example 55.8; GPT-4o-mini GSM8K 90.7 vs 91.9), so the gain is tied to example accuracy, not relevance. Yasunaga's headline 'GPT-3.5 15 vs GPT-4 16' compares GPT-3.5's best variant with plain GPT-4.
agent_test: Run analogical prompting vs plain CoT at equal total tokens; expect gain to shrink.

claim: Self-generated sources help only strong models; for weak models retrieved labelled exemplars are better.
agent_test: Compare self-generated vs retrieved verified source at two model sizes.

claim: Failure audit of analogical prompting (n=100): 28 of 50 wrong answers had a relevant, correct exemplar and still failed (12 generalisation gap, 8 over-reliance on exemplar). The transfer step itself needs a test.
agent_test: Measure how often a correct source plus a wrong transferred conjecture occurs; add a test step.

claim: Thought Propagation (analogous problems solved then aggregated): +12 points optimal shortest paths, +15% agent planning; best ALFWorld variant used real environment trials not a model judge. One layer of analogs gets most of the gain.
agent_test: Replace model-judge aggregation with a test or execution; compare at equal tokens.

claim: Re-representation (naming attributes, decomposing by component) raises transfer accuracy, notably for small models (Raven text: 77.2% with number naming vs at most 51.8% others; decomposition about +20).
agent_test: Compare raw vs structured relational encoding of source and target before mapping.

claim: A model's written rationale for an analogy choice often diverges from its choice (right message, wrong pick; keyword-driven); human justifications are post hoc too. Rationale is not evidence of a checked mapping.
agent_test: Compare accuracy of conjectures accepted on rationale alone vs on test pass.

claim: Solved far-analogy demonstrations help far analogies by close to 10 points for GPT-3.5 and Llama-2 but hurt near ones; GPT-4 stable. Gap not closed.
agent_test: Test with and without far-analogy exemplars on mixed near and far items.

claim: Case-memory retrieval with a learned selection policy adds 4.7 to 9.6 points on out-of-distribution tasks in Memento, confounded by strong planner and tools; no ablation of the mapping step.
agent_test: Ablate case memory on shifted tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Step-by-step written reasoning may hurt analogy transfer (one worked example; DeepSeek R1 solved it by testing alternative rules). Anecdote only.
agent_test: Compare direct answer vs CoT vs rule-testing on a mutated analogy set.

claim: Bartha's two tests give a usable checklist: prior association (a clear link ties the source similarity to the projected feature) and potential for generalisation (no critical disanalogy in the target). Philosophical review, never tested on an agent.
agent_test: Implement as: name the link, search for a target feature that breaks it; measure caught false conjectures.

claim: Systematicity does not guarantee a true inference (Antarctica to Mars example), so a structural score cannot replace an independent test.
agent_test: Check correlation between structure score and verified truth of conjectures.

claim: Model-judged verification and LLM-written counterexample search are weak checks. REFUTE: o3-mini (high) with code feedback finds a valid counterexample for under 9 percent of wrong solutions though it solves up to 48 percent from scratch; 86 percent of its failed random-search attempts come from wrong brute-force code. At equal compute, extra samples with majority vote beat generative verification until about 8x compute (Llama-3.1-8B, MATH). Selective verification gave 76.3 vs 75.5 percent and cut harmful flips 2.2 to 1.0 percent, but a longer first attempt matched it with 28 percent fewer tokens. Same-model self-check is task- and model-dependent. All evidence is on math, code and QA, not on transferred analogical conjectures.
agent_test: Run O7 with (a) no check, (b) model-judged check, (c) executable test or validator, at equal total tokens; count wrong conjectures kept and right ones flipped to wrong.

claim: Reasoning-era models (2025-26) have not closed the transfer gap on related tasks. o3-mini 86.6 to 17.0 and R1 80.6 to 23.2 percent on I-RAVEN-X with noise, despite 3.4x more reasoning tokens; top A2RBench models 39.8 vs humans 68.5 percent; Claude Opus 4.5 and Gemini 3 Pro fall to chance (about 12 percent) as relational complexity grows, with 4k to 16k more thinking tokens adding 0 to 3 points; a chemistry toolkit did not remove the fall. ARN-type far-domain items and mutated letter strings were not re-measured on these models, and a paired with/without-code test is missing.
agent_test: Build far-source and near-decoy items plus mutated letter strings; run a reasoning model with and without code, matched tokens.

claim: Source correctness gates transfer more than relevance does. Self-generated examples that are random but right match relevant ones (accuracy of the example is the key factor, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o-mini). Retrieved labelled analogous cases lift F1 for all six models tested (GPT-4o 43.3 to 75.4), and flipping the labels cuts the result in five of six (GPT-4o 59.2, Qwen3-8B 46.3 below its 50.5 baseline), with Claude 3.7 Sonnet the exception. Similarity-only case retrieval plateaus; outcome-based utility re-ranking adds 3.8 points on average.
agent_test: Same model: self-generated source vs retrieved verified source vs retrieved source with a planted error, at equal tokens.

claim: Unrequested analogical transfer occurs. Humans transfer from an earlier relationally similar passage without awareness (Day and Gentner 2007, abstract only). In code models, a benign metaphorical skill text steers algorithm choice toward the source-domain procedure in 23 to 35 percent of samples versus 3 to 10 percent for literal text (adversarially searched, so an upper bound). O7 should run whenever a source schema is in context, not only when asked.
agent_test: Place a plausible but wrong-domain procedure in context with no analogy request; measure how often its steps appear in the answer, with and without an O7 check.

claim: Surface decoys win when the relation is weakly encoded. In 7-14B open models, failures on story analogies show equal or larger token alignment to the noun-similar distractor than to the true target, and patching the relation fixed up to 38 percent of wrong proportional analogies. One irrelevant sentence leaves at most 18 percent of GSM8K problems solved under every distractor type (2022 models); 20-sample voting and an explicit ignore-instruction recover much. No false-conjecture rate for a relation-level check on decoys was found.
agent_test: Decoy items (surface-similar, structurally wrong source); measure conjecture error with a relation-only check versus none.

claim: A staged analogy-then-solve step beats call-matched baselines on novelty and diversity for Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Flash (binary novelty 50.4 to 68.8 percent vs 21.6 to 37.9 for the cross-domain baseline at 2 calls each). This measures breadth, not correctness of the transferred content; token budgets were not matched.
agent_test: Compare analogy-first with cross-domain-first at equal tokens, scoring validity of kept ideas by a test, not by a judge.
